cls: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor (multi-targeted: VEGFR-1/2/3, PDGFR, c-Kit, FGFR)
quick: 800 mg orally once daily, without food
Take on empty stomach (>=1 h before or 2 h after food)
Can cause fetal harm; avoid, use contraception
No adjustment for mild-moderate; limited data if CrCl <30
Reduce to 200 mg/day (moderate); avoid in severe
LFTs, BP, ECG/electrolytes, thyroid, urine protein
summary: Pazopanib is an oral multi-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor (VEGFR, PDGFR, c-Kit) indicated for advanced renal cell carcinoma and for advanced soft tissue sarcoma after prior chemotherapy. The recommended dose is 800 mg once daily on an empty stomach. It carries a BOXED WARNING for severe and fatal hepatotoxicity, requiring serial liver function monitoring and dose interruption/reduction. Other key risks include hypertension, QT prolongation/torsades, arterial and venous thrombotic events, haemorrhage and GI perforation.
indications: Advanced soft tissue sarcoma (STS) in patients who have received prior chemotherapy

dosage.d: 800 mg orally once daily without food
dosage.n: Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity; do not exceed 800 mg/day

dosage.d: Interrupt; on recovery resume at reduced dose (e.g. 400 mg, then 200 mg)
Consider 400 mg/day; avoid co-administration if possible

admin: Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or split (alters exposure)
Take without food, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal
Take at the same time each day
Separate from drugs that raise gastric pH where possible (reduced absorption)
moa: Pazopanib inhibits multiple receptor tyrosine kinases including vascular endothelial growth factor receptors 1, 2 and 3 (VEGFR), platelet-derived growth factor receptors alpha and beta (PDGFR), fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) and c-Kit. This blocks tumour angiogenesis and proliferation signalling, inhibiting growth of vascularised tumours.

relative: QT prolongation, congenital long QT, or concomitant QT-prolonging drugs
History of arterial thrombosis, recent haemorrhage or GI perforation/fistula
Recent major surgery or non-healing wounds

preg: Based on mechanism and animal data, pazopanib can cause fetal harm and embryo-fetal lethality. Avoid in pregnancy; women of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during and for a period after treatment.
lact: It is not known whether pazopanib is excreted in human milk; because of potential serious adverse effects in the infant, discontinue breastfeeding during treatment.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for mild to moderate renal impairment. There is limited experience in patients with creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min; use with caution.
hepatic: Hepatotoxicity is the principal risk (boxed warning). Reduce to 200 mg once daily in moderate impairment and do not use in severe impairment. Monitor liver chemistries at baseline, at weeks 3, 5, 7 and 9, then at months 3 and 4, and as clinically indicated; interrupt, reduce or discontinue per ALT/bilirubin thresholds.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, ritonavir, clarithromycin) - increased pazopanib levels; avoid or reduce dose
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin) - reduced efficacy; avoid
moderate: Substrates of CYP3A4/2D6/2C8 with narrow index - pazopanib inhibits these enzymes
Proton pump inhibitors / antacids - reduced absorption
minor: P-gp and BCRP substrates - increased exposure possible
interactions.food: Take without food; food increases absorption ~2-fold and exposure. Avoid grapefruit.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; it adds to hepatotoxicity risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Raises ALT/AST/bilirubin; may cause proteinuria, hypothyroidism and QT prolongation.

serious: Arterial and venous thromboembolism (MI, stroke, PE)

monitoring: Liver chemistries at baseline and per schedule (weeks 3,5,7,9; months 3,4)
Baseline and periodic ECG and electrolytes (K, Mg)
Thyroid function and urinalysis for proteinuria
counsel: Take once daily on an empty stomach at the same time each day, and swallow whole
Stop and call your doctor for yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness or right-sided abdominal pain
Avoid grapefruit and limit or avoid alcohol
Use effective contraception; tell your doctor if pregnancy is possible
Report severe diarrhoea, chest pain, weakness, black stools or sudden abdominal pain
pk: Steady state reached within ~3 weeks of daily dosing
Once-daily dosing supported by long half-life
pearls: BOXED WARNING: severe and fatal hepatotoxicity - serial LFT monitoring is mandatory
Must be taken without food; do not crush tablets, as both change exposure
Hypertension is common and usually early - have a BP plan before starting
Hold pazopanib at least 7 days before elective surgery (impaired wound healing)
Check ECG and correct electrolytes; avoid combining with other QT-prolonging drugs
missed: If a dose is missed and it is more than 12 hours until the next dose, the patient should NOT take the missed dose - skip it and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not double up.
overdose: No specific antidote; pazopanib is not removed by dialysis. Overdose may intensify toxicity (hepatic, hypertension, fatigue). Manage with supportive care and monitor liver function, blood pressure and ECG.
